title: A part requested from a vendor reaches the Part Library when it is received
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new part number that no Part Library entry has and no inventory part uses.
  • Have a vendor, vendor A.
  • Create a work order for this test, work order 1, with an approved line.
  • Start on work order 1 (Work Orders in the top bar, then open work order 1).
custom_steps:
1. In the Parts row of the line, click + Add Part.
  2. Type the new part number in Part Number.
  3. Pick the offer to add the typed number as a new part, not an existing result.
  4. Pick Vendor in Source.
  5. Pick any category in Category.
  6. Pick vendor A in Vendor.
  7. Type 10.00 in Cost.
  8. Type 20.00 in Sell Price.
  9. Click Save Part.
  10. Click Parts in the top bar.
  11. Click Part Library in the left menu.
  12. Type the new part number in the Search box.
  13. Click Work Orders in the top bar.
  14. Open work order 1.
  15. Click the Parts tab.
  16. Click Order on the new part request's row.
  17. Click Parts in the top bar.
  18. Click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  19. Open vendor A's purchase order that holds the new part number.
  20. Click Receive.
  21. Type an invoice number in the invoice number field.
  22. Type 1 as the received quantity.
  23. Click Receive on the Receive screen.
  24. Click Parts in the top bar.
  25. Click Part Library in the left menu.
  26. Type the new part number in the Search box.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The "New Part Request" window opens.

Step 2:

  • The typed number is offered to be added as a new part.

Step 3:

  • The new part number is picked.

Step 4:

  • Source shows Vendor.

Step 5:

  • Category shows the category you picked.

Step 6:

  • Vendor shows vendor A.

Step 7:

  • Cost shows 10.00.

Step 8:

  • Sell Price shows 20.00.

Step 9:

  • The window closes and the part request is saved on the line with the new part number.

Step 10:

  • The Parts left menu shows Part Library.

Step 11:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 12:

  • No entry is listed for the new part number: a part request alone does not make one.

Step 13:

  • The Work Orders list opens.

Step 14:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 15:

  • The Parts tab lists the new part request.

Step 16:

  • The part request is ordered from vendor A.

Step 17:

  • The Parts left menu shows Purchase Orders.

Step 18:

  • The Purchase Orders list opens.

Step 19:

  • The purchase order opens with a line for the new part number.

Step 20:

  • The Receive screen opens.

Step 21:

  • The invoice number shows what you typed.

Step 22:

  • The received quantity shows 1.

Step 23:

  • The line is received.

Step 24:

  • The Parts left menu shows Part Library.

Step 25:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 26:

  • One entry is now listed for the new part number: it was made when the requested part was received.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10824 (Story 11, The Part Library Is Browse and Edit Only)

  • S11-R6: “A new Part Library entry is created only from a part number in use: creating an inventory part (S7-R7 and S7-R8), a part request when the requested part is received, a delivery receipt, a core charge, returning a special-order part to inventory, returning a core to inventory, the parts CSV import, and the public API.”
  • S11-N1: “No route, on screen or behind it, produces a Part Library entry with no inventory part, part request, delivery receipt, core charge, return or import row behind it. The one exception is the public API (S11-E3).”

From: Tech plan "Parts Lifecycle Update — Technical Implementation Plan" (7 Oct 2026, written against PRD v22; re-shared by the QA lead on 27 Oct 2026, unchanged), read 27 Oct 2026

  • §1 Clarifications, Q11 Part request entry timing: “PRD corrected: entry created when the requested part is received (S11-R6)”
